target_customer: Independent retailers and SMEs in Malaysia and Southeast Asia buying wholesale stock, plus the brands, distributors and wholesalers who sell to them; later enterprises and government buyers
problem: Wholesale ordering in Malaysia ran on pen and paper and lacked real time connection between suppliers and retailers.
business_model: SaaS subscription for suppliers plus marketplace and embedded trade credit; later B2B eProcurement
product_category: B2B wholesale marketplace and procurement platform

founders.name: Lennise Ng
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO by Digital News Asia (2017 and 2020) and TechCrunch (2022); she and Rahim come from family trading businesses in fast moving consumer goods, per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Aizat Rahim
previous_startups: Infinite Ventures (co-founded 2014 to 2016, acquired by Kern Technology)
Job4Locum (director 2014 to 2016, medical job portal acquired by MIMS)
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists only him as founder; Digital News Asia (October 2017) names him co-founder and COO. Lennise Ng is added as co-founder from Digital News Asia and TechCrunch.

competitors.name: WYDR
competitors.what: Mobile based wholesale marketplace in India connecting manufacturers, distributors, suppliers and retailers
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; described as Dropee's main regional competitor in October 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and order management software; the hard part was onboarding fragmented suppliers and retailers and later credit underwriting, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier catalogues and retailer ordering history create stickiness, and local trade relationships from the founders' family businesses help, but ordering tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No major incumbent absorbed the wedge in Malaysia; other local startups such as Lapasar appear in later competitor lists, and borong rebranded and moved toward enterprise procurement.

market_need_then: Founders saw pen and paper ordering inside their own family wholesale businesses; by January 2022 more than 80,000 SMEs used the platform with over 100M dollars annualized transaction value per TechCrunch.

branding.name_origin: Borong is Malay for wholesale. The company said it wanted the name to remind it of where it started in Malaysia (Business Today, December 2023, via search summary). The earlier name Dropee suited the dropshipping beginnings.
branding.domain_note: Now uses borong.com after the rebrand; earlier dropee.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, neutral, governance and audit readiness focus

branding.brand_signature: Name that literally means wholesale in Malay

rebrands.why: Business outgrew the dropshipping associated name as it served offline retailers and added credit and procurement products

branding.community_and_virality: Recognition as Financial Times fastest growing company in APAC reported by Focus Malaysia; no community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting local language name after the rebrand and notable ranking press, but the pre rebrand Dropee name did not match the business and the new brand is recent.

pivots.from: Dropee: SME wholesale marketplace and ordering SaaS
pivots.to: borong: neutral B2B eProcurement platform for enterprises, government and SMEs with embedded credit
pivots.why: Business grew beyond dropshipping style positioning; embedded trade credit launched November 2020 and enterprise procurement followed

outcome_analysis: Dropee started as an in house ordering tool for the founders' family trading businesses, joined YC in Winter 2020 and reached 80,000 SMEs by January 2022 with a 7M Series A that included 4M of debt. It added trade credit, rebranded to borong in December 2023 and moved toward enterprise procurement, reaching about 80 staff and a Financial Times growth ranking. A Series B of at least 10M was being sought in March 2024; outcome unconfirmed.
notes: Total raised of 8.7M in TechCrunch matches the three rounds recorded (about 8.65M). Series A included 3M equity and 4M debt. The Business Today article returned 403; rebrand details come from search summaries, with the company llms.txt saying only that the rebrand came after 2022. DealStreetAsia (12 March 2024) headline says borong eyes a Series B with at least 10M target; closing was not confirmed so no round recorded. Aggregator investor lists (AppWorks, Petronas Ventures, Ying Fund) conflict and are not used. Founder education not found. The first seed investor list is limited to Vynn Capital, which the 2020 article says led the early 2019 round.
